=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
File: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh
Line or code reference: Lines 91-98 (PR diff truncation Python heredoc) — the `while i > 0 and (data[i] & 0xC0) == 0x80` loop
Problem: UTF-8-safe truncation starts backtracking at `i = cap` (the first EXCLUDED byte) instead of `i = cap - 1` (the last INCLUDED byte). When `cap` lands on a UTF-8 continuation byte, the loop backtracks past the codepoint's leading byte, dropping the entire trailing codepoint plus potentially more continuation bytes than intended.
Why it fails at runtime: When a large PR diff's truncation point (`RB_JUDGE_PR_DIFF_MAX_BYTES`) falls mid-codepoint, the diff body silently loses more content than the cap promises, and the reviewer/judge model sees a truncated diff with the wrong byte count.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: ~line 12906 (inline Python truncation inside the noop-suspicious recovery sweep's PR diff / comment handling) — same `i = cap` backtracking pattern
Problem: UTF-8-safe truncation starts backtracking at `i = cap` instead of `i = cap - 1`.
Why it fails at runtime: When embedded JSON or diff content hits a UTF-8 boundary, the truncation path loses the trailing codepoint.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh
Line or code reference: Line 52 (the `_embed_input_file` function's inline Python truncation heredoc)
Problem: Same off-by-one: `i = cap` inspects the first excluded byte.
Why it fails at runtime: When a PR comment or review comment embed needs truncation at a UTF-8 boundary, the function drops the trailing codepoint.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

File: .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
Line or code reference: ~line 320 (Phase 4 "Wait for review" step, the `LOG_CONTENT=$(…)` to tmpfile refactor region — specifically the `grep -qaF '::notice::Editor returned a safety-policy refusal'` check)
Problem: The refusal-aware grep checks `$LOG_FILE` for the `::notice::` line, but that annotation is emitted on stderr as a GitHub Actions notice; the check is brittle if the annotation prefix or log format changes.
Why it fails at runtime: If the validator ever changes the refusal annotation to a different Actions command prefix, the refusal-specific warning branch never fires and the Telegram alert stays generic.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: Within the standalone stall recovery `retrigger_review` path (~lines 7704-7776)
Problem: The `tg_notify_issue` and counter-increment block was moved so the Telegram alert fires only when `_std_rtr_push_succeeded="true"` and the push actually succeeded via `git push`.
Why it fails at runtime: When the standalone stall recovery skips the empty-commit push due to an in-flight review or head-advanced guard, the operator receives no Telegram alert and must dig into workflow logs to diagnose why the issue stayed stalled.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: `_integration_branch_ahead_of_default` (~lines 2189-2225), specifically the `integration_branch_exists` guard check
Problem: If the integration branch was deleted for reasons other than the legitimate finalize merge path, the helper returns `ahead_by=0`, which callers interpret as "default branch contains integration tip".
Why it fails at runtime: A deleted integration branch silently signals "ahead_by=0" to all callers, causing the orchestrator to declare project completion against a default branch that never received the integration branch's changes.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
